newsitem.title: Vietnam: Hanoi gives Maryland venture new deadline to pay up.
newsitem.headline: Hanoi gives Maryland venture new deadline to pay up.

text.p: Vietnam has given Maryland-based BBI Investment Group until the end of this month to come up with an initial deposit of $2 million for a joint-venture tourism project near Danang city, media reports said Tuesday.
The Ministry of Planning and Investment had threatened to withdraw the license for the $243 million beach resort because BBI had not deposited the funds in the venture's bank account.

"To facilitate the development of the project, the Ministry of Planning and Investment has allowed the foreign partner to extend the deadline for transferring $2 million to the JV company's account ... until 30 November 1996," the Thanh Nien newspaper said.
A ministry official declined to comment on the reports in Thanh Nien and Dau Tu (Investment) magazine, which is controlled by the planning ministry.
BBI President Robert Bernstein told reporters in Hanoi last May that talks with the ministry had succeeded in paving over differences threatening the project.
